<script>
(function () {
  'use strict';
  var $ = function (id) { return document.getElementById(id); };

  var even = new EvenDt();
  var pump = new JobPump();
  var LEVELS = 5;
  var lvBox = [];
  for (var i = 0; i < LEVELS; i++) { var b = document.createElement('i'); $('lv').appendChild(b); lvBox.push(b); }
  var peakLevel = 0;
  function showLevel(l) { for (var i = 0; i < LEVELS; i++) lvBox[i].className = i >= LEVELS - 1 - l ? 'on' : ''; $('lvn').textContent = l; if (l > peakLevel) peakLevel = l; }
  // Level 0 is full quality (all boxes lit); each step down turns one box off. Shorter delays than the defaults, for the demo only.
  var gov = new QualityGovernor({ levels: LEVELS, slowFrames: 40, downDelay: 1500, fastMs: 4000, upDelay: 4000, onChange: showLevel });
  showLevel(0);

  // ----- texture build: one generator, one yield per 16 rows. The ImageData is created and used inside one slice (nothing shared is held across a yield).
  var SIZE = 2048, ROWS = 16;
  var big = document.createElement('canvas'); big.width = big.height = SIZE;
  var bigG = big.getContext('2d');
  var prevC = $('prev'), prevG = prevC.getContext('2d');
  var building = false, sliceDone = 0, sliceTotal = SIZE / ROWS;
  function hash(x, y) { var h = (x * 374761393 + y * 668265263) | 0; h = (h ^ (h >>> 13)) * 1274126177 | 0; return ((h ^ (h >>> 16)) >>> 0) / 4294967296; }
  function vnoise(x, y) {
    var xi = Math.floor(x), yi = Math.floor(y), xf = x - xi, yf = y - yi;
    var u = xf * xf * (3 - 2 * xf), v = yf * yf * (3 - 2 * yf);
    var a = hash(xi, yi), c = hash(xi + 1, yi), d = hash(xi, yi + 1), e = hash(xi + 1, yi + 1);
    return a + (c - a) * u + (d - a) * v + (a - c - d + e) * u * v;
  }
  function* buildTexture() {
    for (var y0 = 0; y0 < SIZE; y0 += ROWS) {
      var img = bigG.createImageData(SIZE, ROWS), px = img.data, o = 0;
      for (var y = 0; y < ROWS; y++) for (var x = 0; x < SIZE; x++) {
        var n = 0, amp = .5, f = 1 / 160;
        for (var k = 0; k < 5; k++) { n += vnoise(x * f + k * 7, (y0 + y) * returning such an object. Default off: the hint says A, B and Start.
 *   hintMs              how long the hint stays up after waking or a scope change, default 3500
 *   guardMs             A is ignored this long after a scope appears (so the A that opened a panel does not also pick inside it), default 450
 *   wakeMs              a scope that opens within this long of pad use gets focus immediately, default 8000
 *   scroll              keep the focused element visible with scrollIntoView, default true
 *   requireStandard     only read pads whose mapping is 'standard', default true
 *
 * step() never throws: getGamepads (which throws a SecurityError when the page disables the feature) and every callback
 * above are wrapped, and the error goes to onError and pn.lastError.
 */
(function (root, factory) {
  if (typeof module === 'object' && module.exports) module.exports = factory();
  else root.PadNav = factory();
})(typeof self !== 'undefined' ? self : this, function () {
  'use strict';

  var EMPTY = [];

  function PadNav(o) {
    o = o || {};
    var num = function (v, d) { return typeof v === 'number' && isFinite(v) ? v : d; };
    this.getScopeFn = typeof o.getScope === 'function' ? o.getScope : null;
    this.scopeSelector = o.scopeSelector || null;
    this.selector = o.focusableSelector || PadNav.DEFAULT_SELECTOR;
    this.filter = typeof o.filter === 'function' ? o.filter : null;
    this.onBack = o.onBack || null;
    this.onStart = o.onStart || null;
    this.onA = o.onA || null;
    this.onUse = o.onUse || null;
    this.onDisconnect = o.onDisconnect || null;
    this.onError = o.onError || null;
    this.getPads = typeof o.getPads === 'function' ? o.getPads : function () { return typeof navigator !== 'undefined' && navigator.getGamepads ? navigator.getGamepads() : []; };
    this.deadzone = num(o.deadzone, 0.45);
    this.release = typeof o.release === 'number' && isFinite(o.release) ? Math.max(0, o.release) : null;   // null: deadzone - 0.1
    this.repeatDelay = num(o.repeatDelay, 380);
    this.repeatRate = num(o.repeatRate, 120);
    this.focusClass = o.focusClass || 'pad-focus';
    this.formControls = o.formControls !== false;
    this.adjustClass = o.adjustClass || 'pad-adjust';
    this.hintEl = o.hintEl || null;
    this.hintText = o.hintText || null;
    this.labels = o.labels || null;
    this.hintMs = num(o.hintMs, 3500);
    this.guardMs = num(o.guardMs, 450);
    this.wakeMs = num(o.wakeMs, 8000);
    this.scroll = o.scroll !== false;
    this.requireStandard = o.requireStandard !== false;

    this.prev = {};            // last frame's pressed state, for edge detection
    this.rep = {};             // per direction: when the next repeat is due
    this.latch = {};           // per pad: which stick directions are held (for the press/release gap)
    this.hadPad = false;       // was a usable pad read on the latest frame
    this.awake = false;        // true after the first pad input; nothing is shown before that
    this.lastUsed = -Infinity; // time of the latest pad input
    this.useId = '';           // id text of the pad that gave the latest input
    this.seen = false;         // has a scope been looked at yet
    this.scope = null;
    this.scopeAt = -Infinity;
    this.hintAt = 0;
    this.ringEl = null;        // the element wearing focusClass
    this.adjust = null;        // the slider in adjust mode, if any
    this.memory = typeof WeakMap === 'function' ? new WeakMap() : null;   // last focused element per scope
    this.raf = 0;
    this.hintShown = null;     // cached so the DOM is only written when the hint changes
    this.hintShownText = null;
    this.lastError = null;
    this.lastErrorWhere = '';
    this.errKey = '';
    this.nameFor = null;       // cached button names for the pad id in nameFor
    this.nameObj = null;
    this.hintCache = null;

    var self = this;
    this.onBlur = function (e) { if (e.target && e.target === self.ringEl) self.clearRing(); };
    this.onGpGone = function () { self.checkLost(); };
    if (typeof document !== 'undefined') document.addEventListener('blur', this.onBlur, true);
    if (typeof window !== 'undefined' && window.addEventListener) window.addEventListener('gamepaddisconnected', this.onGpGone);
    try {
      var h = this.hintEl;
      if (h && h.setAttribute && !(h.getAttribute && h.getAttribute('role'))) h.setAttribute('role', 'status');   // announced politely; the look is unchanged
    } catch (e) { /* not an element */ }
    this.setHint(false, '');
  }

  /** Pure helper: index of the nearest rect from `from` in direction 'l','r','u' or 'd', or -1. Rects are {left, top, width, height}. */
  PadNav.nearest = function (from, rects, dir) {
    var cx = from.left + from.width / 2, cy = from.top + from.height / 2, best = -1, bs = Infinity, i, p, dx, dy, along, across, score;
    for (i = 0; i < rects.length; i++) {
      p = rects[i]; dx = p.left + p.width / 2 - cx; dy = p.top + p.height / 2 - cy;
      along = dir === 'l' ? -dx : dir === 'r' ? dx : dir === 'u' ? -dy : dy;
      across = dir === 'l' || dir === 'r' ? Math.abs(dy) : Math.abs(dx);
      if (along < 4) continue;                  // not really in that direction (also skips the element itself)
      score = along + across * 2.5;             // sideways drift costs 2.5x: a roughly straight neighbor beats a nearer diagonal one
      if (score < bs) { bs = score; best = i; }
    }
    return best;
  };

  /**
   * Pure stick state machine. x, y are axes 0 and 1; `was` holds last frame's {l, r, u, d} (0 or 1) for this stick;
   * a direction starts above `press` and lets go only below `release`. The stick counts along its stronger axis only.
   * Writes into `out` (may be the same object as `was`) and returns it, so a caller can reuse one object per pad.
   */
  PadNav.stick = function (x, y, was, press, release, out) {
    var ex = Math.abs(x), ey = Math.abs(y);
    was = was || {}; out = out || {};
    if (!(release <= press)) release = press;
    var wl = was.l, wr = was.r, wu = was.u, wd = was.d;
    out.u = y < 0 && ey >= ex && ey > (wu ? release : press) ? 1 : 0;
    out.d = y > 0 && ey >= ex && ey > (wd ? release : press) ? 1 : 0;
    out.l = x < 0 && ex > ey && ex > (wl ? release : press) ? 1 : 0;
    out.r = x > 0 && ex > ey && ex > (wr ? release : press) ? 1 : 0;
    return out;
  };

  /** Pure: decimal places a number needs when written out (0.25 gives 2). */
  PadNav.decimals = function (n) {
    var m = /(?:\.(\d+))?(?:e-(\d+))?$/.exec(String(n));
    return m ? (m[1] ? m[1].length : 0) + (m[2] ? +m[2] : 0) : 0;
  };

  /**
   * Pure: the slider value after one step in direction dir (1 or -1), as a string. Arguments are the input's value, min, max
   * and step strings. HTML defaults apply: min 0, max 100, step 1; step "any" uses one hundredth of the range.
   */
  PadNav.rangeNext = function (value, min, max, step, dir) {
    var lo = parseFloat(min), hi = parseFloat(max), st = parseFloat(step), v = parseFloat(value), n;
    if (!isFinite(lo)) lo = 0;
    if (!isFinite(hi)) hi = 100;
    if (hi < lo) hi = lo;
    if (!(st > 0) || !isFinite(st)) st = String(step).toLowerCase() === 'any' && hi > lo ? (hi - lo) / 100 : 1;
    if (!isFinite(v)) v = lo;
    n = v + (dir < 0 ? -st : st);
    if (n < lo) n = lo;
    if (n > hi) n = hi;
    return String(Number(n.toFixed(Math.min(20, Math.max(PadNav.decimals(st), PadNav.decimals(lo), PadNav.decimals(v))))));
  };

  /** Pure: index of the next enabled option after `cur`, wrapping around; `cur` itself if it is the only enabled one; -1 if none. opts is an array-like of {disabled}. */
  PadNav.nextOption = function (opts, cur) {
    var n = opts ? opts.length : 0, j, k;
    for (j = 1; j <= n; j++) {
      k = ((cur < 0 ? -1 : cur) + j) % n;
      if (opts[k] && !opts[k].disabled) return k;
    }
    return -1;
  };

  /** Pure: button names for the default hint, guessed from a pad's id text (not standardized, so it is a guess). Always returns a new object { dpad, a, b, start }. */
  PadNav.labelsFor = function (id) {
    var s = String(id || '').toLowerCase(), o = { dpad: 'D-pad', a: 'A', b: 'B', start: 'Start' };
    if (/playstation|dualshock|dualsense|sony|054c|\bps[345]\b/.test(s)) { o.a = 'Cross'; o.b = 'Circle'; o.start = 'Options'; }
    else if (/nintendo|057e|joy-?con|pro controller|switch/.test(s)) { o.a = 'B'; o.b = 'A'; o.start = '+'; }   // the standard layout is by position: index 0 is the bottom button, printed B on Nintendo pads
    return o;
  };

  PadNav.clock = function () { return typeof performance !== 'undefined' && performance.now ? performance.now() : Date.now(); };

  /** Call once per frame. nowMs defaults to performance.now(). Returns true if a usable pad was read. Never throws. */
  PadNav.prototype.step = function (nowMs) {
    try { return this.run(typeof nowMs === 'number' ? nowMs : PadNav.clock()); }
    catch (e) { this.fail('step', e); return false; }
  };

  PadNav.prototype.run = fu# frame-kit

Test everything (Node only, offline, about a second): `node modules/frame-kit/test/run.js` (run from the repository root; it exits non-zero on any failure).
Browser check of the example (Playwright for Python, Chromium already installed): `python3 modules/frame-kit/test/check-example.py`.

## What it is

Four tiny, independent helpers for browser games and other `requestAnimationFrame` loops. Each is one file with no dependencies; use any one without the others.

| Helper | File | One line |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `EvenDt` | `even-dt.js` | Smooths the uneven frame gaps a browser reports by snapping them to the screen's learned refresh period. |
| `QualityGovernor` | `quality-governor.js` | Steps a quality level down or up from how long frames really take, with hysteresis. |
| `JobPump` | `job-pump.js` | Runs queued build steps for about N milliseconds per frame, so a big pre-render never hitches a frame. |
| `FrameMeter` | `frame-meter.js` | A speed meter: frames a second, the slowest frame, hitches with a plain-words cause (game or device) and the delay from a tap to the next frame. |

## Why it exists

- Browsers report frame gaps that wobble by a millisecond or two even when every frame is presented on time. A game that moves by the raw gap shows that wobble as a faint shiver in scrolling scenery. `EvenDt` removes most of it.
- Screens differ: a game that is fine at full quality on one machine needs fewer particles or a lower canvas resolution on another. `QualityGovernor` decides when to change level; you decide what a level means.
- Procedural art, texture atlases and other bakes can take hundreds of milliseconds. Done in one go they freeze the page. `JobPump` lets you write the bake as a function or a generator and spreads it over frames.

They were extracted from a real, shipped single-file browser game and rewritten to stand alone.

## Quick start

Open `demo.html` by double-click to see all four working (sections 2 and 4 each have a one-button automatic check that reports in plain words). To use them, copy the files you want:

```html
<script src="even-dt.js"></script>
<script src="quality-governor.js"></script>
<script src="job-pump.js"></script>
<script src="frame-meter.js"></script>        <!-- optional: see the FrameMeter section below -->
<script>
  const even = new EvenDt();
  const pump = new JobPump();
  const gov = new QualityGovernor({
    levels: 3,                                   // levels 0 (full), 1, 2 (lightest)
    onChange: (level) => console.log('quality level is now', level)
  });

  // A big bake written as a generator: one slice per yield.
  const texture = document.createElement('canvas');
  texture.width = texture.height = 1024;
  pump.add(function* () {
    const g = texture.getContext('2d');
    for (let y = 0; y < 1024; y += 32) {
      g.fillStyle = 'hsl(' + (y / 4) + ',60%,50%)';
      g.fillRect(0, y, 1024, 32);
      yield;                                     // give the frame back
    }
  });

  let last = 0;
  function frame(now) {
    if (last) {
      const gap = now - last;
      const dtMs = even.next(gap);               // smoothed gap for movement
      gov.frame(gap, now);                       // real gap for the governor
      pump.run(4);                               // about 4 ms of build work per frame
      // ... move things by dtMs / 1000 seconds, then draw ...
    }
    last = now;
    requestAnimationFrame(frame);
  }
  requestAnimationFrame(frame);
</script>
```

In Node (for tests): `const EvenDt = require('./even-dt.js');`. Each file works both ways (browser global and `module.exports`, through the usual UMD wrapper at the top of the file).

Pasting a file into a single-file game is fine: its `'use strict'` is inside the wrapper, so it does not make the rest of your script strict.

## API

All options are optional. Defaults are the values from the original game.

### `new EvenDt(opts)`

| Member | Meaning |
| --- | --- |
| `.next(gapMs)` | Returns the smoothed gap in ms. A value that is not a positive finite number returns `0`. |
| `.period` | The learned screen period in ms (median of the recent gaps), `0` while warming up. |
| `.drift` | Milliseconds currently owed, for debugging. |
| `.reset()` | Forget everything (use after a long pause or when the window moves to another screen). |

How `next()` works: gaps of `minGap` or less and `maxGap` or more are returned unchanged and not learned from. Otherwise the gap goes into a window of the last `window` gaps. After `warmup` gaps the period is the median of the window (recomputed every `refreshEvery` gaps). A gap is rounded to the nearest whole multiple of the period (1 to `maxMultiple`); if it is within `tolerance` of the period from that multiple it becomes the multiple plus a small pay-back, otherwise it is returned unchanged and the owed drift is dropped. The difference between the raw gap and the multiple is added to a drift account, of which `payback` is paid out each frame.

| Option | Default | Meaning |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `minGap` | `2` | Ignore gaps at or below this (ms). On a screen near 480 Hz or faster pass `0.5` (see the limits below). |
| `maxGap` | `60` | Ignore gaps at or above this (ms): tab switches, long stalls. |
| `window` | `40` | How many recent gaps the median covers. |
| `warmup` | `12` | Gaps needed before snapping starts. |
| `refreshEvery` | `8` | Recompute the median every this many gaps. |
| `maxMultiple` | `3` | Largest multiple of the period to snap to (2 is a dropped frame). |
| `tolerance` | `0.3` | A gap snaps only within this fraction of the period from a multiple. |
| `payback` | `0.04` | Fraction of the owed drift paid back per frame. |

### `new QualityGovernor(opts)`

| Member | Meaning |
| --- | --- |
| `.frame(gapMs, nowMs)` | Feed every frame: the real gap and the current time from any steady clock. |
| `.level` | Current level, `0` (full quality) to `levels - 1` (lightest). |
| `.average` | The smoothed frame gap in ms, for a debug overlay. |
| `.force(n)` | Jump to level `n` (clamped). Restarts the streaks, the delay clock and the flip-flop guard, and calls `onChange` if the level changed. |
| `.hold()` | Drop the current slow and fast streaks. Call it while frames are not representative (menu open, tab hidden). |
| `.flips` | How many quick reversals (a step up, then a step down soon after) the flip-flop guard has seen. |
| `.gaveUp` | `true` once the guard has given up on a level: the governor stays below it. |
| `.resetGuard()` | Forget the reversals and the give-ups, so every level may be tried again. |
| `.lastError` | The last error thrown by `onChange`, or `null`. |
| `.enabled` | Set to `false` to freeze the governor. |

The rule: an exponential moving average of the gap (`smoothing`) is compared with `slowAbove` and `fastBelow`. It must stay above `slowAbove` for `slowFrames` frames in a row, and `downDelay` ms must have passed since the last change, to step down one level (the average tx; }
  p { margin: 6px 0; }
  .muted { opacity: .75; font-size: 14px; }
  .panel { background: var(--card); border: 1px solid var(--line); border-radius: 12px; padding: 16px; margin: 16px 0; max-height: 300px; overflow: auto; }
  .panel[hidden] { display: none; }
  .panel h2 { font-size: 18px; margin: 0 0 10px; }
  .row { display: flex; flex-wrap: wrap; gap: 10px; }
  button { font: inherit; padding: 10px 16px; border-radius: 8px; border: 1px solid var(--line); background: var(--bg); color: var(--fg); cursor: pointer; }
  .list button { display: block; width: 100%; text-align: left; margin-bottom: 8px; }
  /* The focus ring pad-nav puts on the focused element. You style it; the library only adds the class. */
  .pad-focus { outline: 3px solid var(--accent); outline-offset: 2px; }
  .pad-adjust { outline-style: dashed; }   /* a slider in adjust mode: left and right change it */
  .ctl { display: flex; align-items: center; gap: 10px; margin-bottom: 8px; padding: 6px 0; }
  .ctl input[type=range] { flex: 1; }
  #hint { position: sticky; bottom: 8px; margin: 8px 0; padding: 8px 12px; border-radius: 8px; background: var(--accent); color: #fff; font-size: 14px; }
  #hint[hidden] { display: none; }
  #sim { display: grid; grid-template-columns: repeat(3, 56px); gap: 6px; justify-content: start; margin: 8px 0; user-select: none; touch-action: none; }
  #sim button { padding: 8px 0; text-align: center; }
  #sim .gap { visibility: hidden; }
  .simrow { display: flex; gap: 6px; margin: 6px 0; }
  #status { font-size: 14px; }
  #log { font: 13px/1.4 ui-monospace, monospace; background: var(--card); border: 1px solid var(--line); border-radius: 8px; padding: 8px 12px; height: 120px; overflow: auto; white-space: pre-wrap; }
</style>
